subject: Maths
title: Rounding to significant figures
subtitle: Place Value and Ordering Integers · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can round numbers to a given number of significant figures.

key_vocab.definition: Significant figures (s.f.) are counted from the first non-zero digit. Leading zeros are not significant but trailing zeros after a decimal point are.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can round numbers to a given number of significant figures.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Significant figures -- Significant figures (s.f.) are counted from the first non-zero digit. Leading zeros are not significant but trailing zeros after a decimal point are.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Count significant figures from the first non-zero digit. Round using normal rounding rules.
0.00473 to 2 s.f. = 0.0047
Leading zeros are placeholders, not significant

Key examples:
  ✓ 3462 to 2 s.f. = 3500  (round up (6 ≥ 5))
  ✓ 0.00587 to 2 s.f. = 0.0059  (leading zeros not significant)
  ✓ 45.83 to 1 s.f. = 50  (round up (5 ≥ 5))
  ✗ 0.00587 to 2 s.f. = 0.01  (counted the zeros as significant)
  ✗ 3462 to 2 s.f. = 3400  (should round up, not down)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – rounding whole numbers
  Round 5738 to 2 significant figures.
  First 2 s.f.: 5, 7
  Next digit is 3 (< 5), so round down
  = 5700
  = 5700
  (Fill remaining places with zeros to keep the number the right size.)

Example 2 – rounding decimals
  Round 0.04562 to 2 significant figures.
  Skip leading zeros: first s.f. is 4, second is 5
  Next digit is 6 (≥ 5), so round up
  = 0.046
  = 0.046
  (Leading zeros are not counted as significant.)

sections.title: Mixed rounding
sections.content:
Round to the number of significant figures stated.

(a) 8765 to 1 s.f.
(b) 0.00456 to 2 s.f.
(c) 345.67 to 3 s.f.
(d) 0.9996 to 3 s.f.

sections.title: Significant figures in context
sections.content:
Round each value appropriately.

(a) A distance of 12,345 m to 2 s.f.
(b) A mass of 0.00872 kg to 2 s.f.
(c) A population of 67,530 to 3 s.f.
(d) A speed of 345.8 m/s to 2 s.f.
(e) A probability of 0.4567 to 3 s.f.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 0.0047 has 2 significant figures
✗ The zero in 3.02 is not significant
✓ 5738 to 2 s.f. = 5700
✗ Leading zeros count as significant figures
✓ When rounding up 9, it becomes 10 and carries
